extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians in arithmetic geometry and number theory (readers of Mochizuki's IUT theory)
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts and applies precise metric/log-volume estimates and structure theorems (nonarchimedean and archimedean) used in Inter-Universal Teichmüller Theory, together with supporting facts about torsion points of elliptic curves and arithmetic divisors required to bound packet-normalized log-volumes of Θ-pilot objects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonarchimedean normalized log-volume (normalization rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: The log-volumes constructed in [AbsTopIII], Proposition 5.7, (i), on finite extensions of Q_p may be normalized (by dividing by degree of the extension) to yield μlog(−) defined on compact open subsets of finite extensions of Q_p contained in Q_p, valued in R, and normalized so that μlog(R_i) = 0, μlog(p · R_i) = −log(p) for each i ∈ I. This notion extends to compact open subsets of tensor products of finitely many finite extensions, normalized so that μlog((R_E)∼) = 0, μlog(p · (R_E)∼) = −log(p) for any nonempty E ⊆ I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply normalization by dividing by the degree of the finite extension. Compatibility with tensor-product decompositions is used to define μlog on tensor products; normalization choices (μlog(R)=0, μlog(pR) = −log p) are explicitly required when computing or comparing log-volumes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formula for μlog(log_p(R×_i))
rubrics_metrics.description: For each i, μlog(log_p(R×_i)) = −(1/ e_i + m_i/(e_i f_i)) · log(p) (equivalently −(f_i + m_i)·log(p) after the displayed simplification in the text).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This follows from compatibility of μlog with log_p(−) and the basic properties of the nonarchimedean log-volume in [AbsTopIII], Proposition 5.7. Use the given relation between torsion subgroup order p^{m_i}·(p^{f_i}−1) and the normalization to compute the displayed expression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusions and upper bounds for scaled logp modules (Prop. 1.4(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Given I* ⊆ I with certain ei constraints (for i ∈ I  ackslash I* one has p−2 ≥ e_i), then for any λ ∈ (1/e_i)·Z and a chosen i† ∈ I there are inclusions φ(p^{λ} · (R_I)∼) ⊆ p^{λ−d_I−a_I} · log_p(R×_I) ⊆ p^{λ−d_I−a_I−b_I} · (R_I)∼ together with explicit upper bounds on μlog of these sets: μlog(p^{λ−d_I−a_I}·log_p(R×_I)) ≤ (−λ + d_I + 1 + 4·|I*|/p)·log(p) (and a more refined displayed inequality involving μlog(log_p(R×_I)) and terms ∑_{i∈I*}{3 + log(e_i)}). Also d_I + a_I ≥ |I| if p>2, and ≥ 2·|I| if p=2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These inclusions and inequalities account for indeterminacies and automorphisms (φ) and provide concrete upper bounds for the log-volume of sets that contain the possible images of Θ-pilot objects; the bounds depend on combinatorial data (|I|, |I*|), ramification invariants (e_i), and integer parameters d_I,a_I,b_I. Use the displayed inequalities directly when bounding μlog of scaled log_p-modules; note special simplifications when all e_i = 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special case: trivial ramification (Prop. 1.4(iv))
rubrics_metrics.description: If p > 2 and e_i = 1 for all i ∈ I then φ((R_I)∼) ⊆ (R_I)∼ and μlog((R_I)∼) = 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When all local ramification indices equal 1 (and p>2), the normalized log-volume of the integral structure vanishes and the automorphism φ preserves the integral structure; use this to obtain exact vanishing contributions in global estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Archimedean: tensor vs direct-sum metric compatibility (Prop. 1.5(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Hermitian metric on C determines a tensor-product metric on C⊗_R C and a direct-sum metric on C⊕C; the Chinese-remainder-type isomorphism C⊗_R C ≅ C⊕C is compatible with these metrics up to a factor of 2, i.e., the metric on the right corresponds to 2 times the metric on the left (so lengths differ by factor √2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When comparing metrics arising from tensor products and direct sums over R in archimedean places, include the multiplicative factor 2 (or √2 on lengths) in any norm/length comparisons; this constant propagates through subsequent metric-volume calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Archimedean: automorphism compatibility (Prop. 1.5(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Relative to the decomposition C⊗_R C ≅ C⊕C and the metrics of (i), the direct-sum decomposition C⊕C (with its Hermitian metric) is preserved (up to the stated metric factor) by automorphisms of C⊗_R C induced by primitive automorphisms (complex conjugation and multiplication by ±1, ±√−1) of the factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primitive automorphisms act compatibly with the direct-sum/tensor-product metric structures; when accounting for symmetries in archimedean contributions include invariance under these automorphisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Archimedean: direct-sum/tensor product scaling and integral structure (Prop. 1.5(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: For finite nonempty sets I,V and M = ⊕_{v∈V} C_v, the tensor-product M_I = ⊗_{i∈I} M_i has a unique direct-sum decomposition as a direct sum of 2^{|I|−1} · |V|^{|I|} copies of C; the direct-sum metric equals 2^{|I|−1} times the original tensor-product metric on M_I. The integral structure B_I (the direct product of unit balls of the C summands) is preserved by automorphisms induced by primitive automorphisms of the summands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the explicit combinatorial factor 2^{|I|−1} when converting between tensor-product and direct-sum metrics and when defining unit-ball/integral structures at archimedean places; these factors contribute multiplicatively to archimedean metric/log-volume estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Archimedean: tensor product of vectors of given length (Prop. 1.5(iv))
rubrics_metrics.description: If in the situation of (iii) each vector m_i ∈ M_i has components in each direct summand Cv of length λ > 0, then ⊗_{i∈I} m_i ∈ λ^{|I|} · B_I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When forming tensor products of vectors whose components have fixed length, their tensor lies in the integral structure scaled by λ^{|I|}; apply this to bound archimedean contributions to holomorphic hull volumes by powers of component lengths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prime number estimate (Prop. 1.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: There exists n_0 such that for all n ≥ n_0, n ≤ 4 p_n /(3 · log p_n). Equivalently, lim_{n→∞} n·log(p_n)/p_n = 1, hence there is η_prm > 0 such that for all η ≥ η_prm an inequality of the displayed form (summing primes p ≤ η) holds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this quantitative form of the prime number theorem to bound sums/products over primes and to produce explicit numeric constants (η_prm) that appear in global log-volume bounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weighted-averages identity (Prop. 1.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given finite nonempty E, n ≥1, weights λ_e ∈ R_{>0}, coefficients β_e ∈ R, define β_avg = β_E/λ_E with β_E = ∑_{e∈E} β_e·λ_e, λ_E = ∑_{e∈E} λ_e, and for n-tuples define β^(e) = ∑_{j=1}^n β_{e_j}, λ^Π(e) = ∏_{j=1}^n λ_{e_j}. Then for any i =1,...,n the displayed equalities hold which imply n·β_avg equals the symmetric sum over E^n of β^{(e)}·λ^Π(e)/λ^Π(e) etc (the displayed identities in the proposition).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these combinatorial identities to pass from componentwise bounds to symmetrized (packet-normalized) averages; the identity is applied in the paper to compute packet-normalized log-volumes by symmetrizing over choices of indices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement rule for normalized weights (Remark 1.7.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: When working with normalized log-volumes (as in Prop. 1.4(i)) the normalized weights appearing in [IUTchIII], Remark 3.1.1(ii) must be replaced by expressions of the form [K_v : Q_v^Q]·[K_v : (Fmod)_v]^{-1} = [(Fmod)_v : Q_v^Q], and more generally by the λ-product expressions appearing in Prop. 1.7 where λ_e = [(Fmod)_v : Q_v^Q] and β_e is a normalized log-volume of some compact open subset of K_v.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When converting prior (non-normalized) weight formulas to the present normalized-log-volume normalization, systematically replace weights by the indicated degree ratios; this affects packet-normalized averaging and must be applied whenever using Proposition 1.7 to average local estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arithmetic divisor definitions and normalized degree (Definition 1.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: An R-arithmetic divisor a on a number field F is a finite formal sum a = ∑_{v∈V(F)} c_v·v with c_v ∈ R; support Supp(a) = {v | c_v ≠ 0}. The degree map deg_F : ADiv_R(F) → R is given by v_nonarch → log q_v and v_arch → 1; the normalized degree is deg(a) = (1/[F:Q])·deg_F(a). For E a set of valuations over v_Q ∈ V(Q), define a_E = ∑_{v∈E} c_v·v and the normalized E-degree deg_E(a) = deg(a_E)/[F_v : Q_{v_Q}^Q]. Pullback/invariance: deg(a|_K) = deg(a) for finite extensions K/F (with natural pullback).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these normalized-degree conventions throughout; note the scaling by local extension degrees when forming deg_E and when comparing divisors across extensions. The paper uses these conventions repeatedly in global log-volume inequalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serre's criterion for automorphisms on l-torsion (Prop. 1.8(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Let l ≥ 3 be a prime invertible in a perfect field k and A an abelian variety over k with polarization λ. The natural map φ: Aut_k(A,λ) → Aut(A[l]) is injective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this injectivity to deduce finiteness or rigidity of automorphism groups from l-level structure information; it is invoked to show certain stacks become schemes or to control ramification in level-structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automorphism exact sequence and field of definition (Prop. 1.8(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: For an elliptic curve E_k over algebraic closure k of k, there is a natural exact sequence 1 → Aut_k(E_k) → Aut_k(E_k) → G_k (image G_E open) and natural representations ρ_n : Aut_k(E_k) → Aut(E_k[n]). The minimal field of definition k_E equals the fixed field determined by G_E, and descent data for models over subextensions corresponds to sections of Aut_k(E_k) → G_k over closed subgroups H ⊆ G_k.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this exact sequence and representation to relate automorphism groups, Galois actions on torsion, and fields of definition; it guides descent arguments and the construction of models with prescribed torsion rationality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factorization of ρ_2 when automorphism group is ±1 (Prop. 1.8(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: If Aut_k(E_k) = {±1}, then the representation ρ_2 factors through G_E and hence defines a natural representation G_E → Aut(E_k[2]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This allows control of 2-torsion Galois action when automorphism group is minimal; used to deduce descent and explicit model forms (Legendre) under further hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Descent when l-torsion is rational (Prop. 1.8(iv))
rubrics_metrics.description: If l ≥ 3 is invertible in k and E_k descends to elliptic curves all of whose l-torsion points are rational over k, then E_k descends to a model defined over k (i.e., admitting all l-torsion rational over k).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The combination of injectivity from (i) and the torsion-rational assumption yields a unique closed subgroup providing descent; apply this when level-structure rationality is known to produce models over the base field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Semi-stable reduction from rational l-torsion (Prop. 1.8(v))
rubrics_metrics.description: If k is a complete discrete valuation field with ring Ok, l ≥ 3 invertible in Ok, and E_k descends to an elliptic curve over k whose l-torsion points are rational over k, then that model has semi-stable reduction over Ok (i.e., extends to a semi-abelian scheme).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this to control local reduction types when torsion rationality is present; feeds into ramification/different/conductor bounds used in global divisor/log-volume estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legendre form descent and quadratic twisting (Prop. 1.8(vi))
rubrics_metrics.description: If Aut_k(E_k) = {±1}, 2 is invertible in k, G_E = G_k, and the representation G_E → Aut(E_k[2]) is trivial, then E_k descends (possibly after a quadratic twist) to an elliptic curve over k definable by the Legendre form. If further k is a complete DVR with 2 invertible in Ok, then E_k has semi-stable reduction over some quadratic extension of k of degree ≤ 2; if E_k has good reduction then no extension is necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under the listed hypotheses, explicit Legendre-model descent is available and gives strong control on local reduction behavior; use this when constructing explicit models to bound conductor/q-parameters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unramified/tame ramification for torsion action vs reduction (Prop. 1.8(vii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Let k be a complete DVR with ring Ok and n invertible in Ok. If a model E_k has good reduction then the action of G_k on E_k[n] is unramified. If E_k has bad multiplicative reduction then the kernel of G_k action on E_k[n] determines a tamely ramified extension whose ramification index over k divides n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This links reduction type to ramification of torsion Galois representations and is used to identify distinguished places that ramify in the global extension determined by torsion level structures; apply when relating conductors/different divisors to ramification behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Packet-normalized log-volume inequality for Θ-pilot objects (Theorem 1.10 summary)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the stated initial Θ-data and hypotheses (elliptic curve E_F has good reduction outside V(F)_good not dividing 2l, specified tripodal and torsion-field extensions F_mod⊆F_tpd⊆F etc.), there is an explicit upper bound of the form (displayed in text) giving a linear inequality relating (1/6)·log(q) and a combination of (1 + const·d_mod / l)·(log(d_{Ftpd}) + log(f_{Ftpd})) + const·(e^*_mod · l + η_prm), where constants and the full displayed expression are as in the theorem (the paper gives an explicit C_Θ and then deduces the displayed inequality bounding log(q)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This theorem assembles the nonarchimedean and archimedean estimates, ramification and conductor/divisor inequalities, weighted-averaging, and prime-number-theorem constants to give a global effective inequality bounding the normalized degree (log q) in terms of local/inertial arithmetic invariants. When applying to Θ-pilot objects, plug in the explicit values (d_mod, e^*_mod, log(d_{Ftpd}), log(f_{Ftpd}), η_prm) to obtain numeric bounds.
